title: Coefficient transport of the two independent support identity units
statement: For a finite commutative ring A, an open immersion i:X→Z and a proper map p:Z→Y, the canonical coefficient compact-support comparisons commute with the independently defined identity-factor unit isomorphism of [lem-sf-identity-factor-fixed-support]. For every ordinary fixed-ULift A pro-etale derived object M, first apply intrinsic proper support to the open coefficient comparison, then the proper coefficient comparison, then coefficient realization of identityFactorFixedIso. This equals the proper candidate identity map, intrinsic proper image of the open candidate identity map, and the coefficient comparison for the actual pair (i,p). The maps and comparisons are precisely those of [def-sf-operation-stages]. No etale origin, chosen geometric compositor, field datum, or positive-level witness occurs.

proof.text: For any adjunction and equivalence, calculate the identity left-adjoint comparison using the transported unit. Specializing to extension by zero identifies sfIntrinsicOpenId with transport of openImmersionLowerShriekIdIso. Apply the existing exact-derived identity-square theorem to sfIntrinsicOpenExtensionComparison; naturality of the identity open map and the equivalence triangle give open_identity_square.

Calculate the right-adjoint identity map through the transported adjunction and the specified underived direct-image comparison. The fixed-scalar right identity is lowerStarId by its conjugation characterization. Prove that deriving an adjunction with an identified identity left functor gives the right-derived natural identity isomorphism, using the derived counit normalization on the homotopy localization. Finally apply the all-complex inverse direct-image normalization: cancel the exact identity direct-image derived unit and the realization factor, and use the underived square degreewise. This proves direct_identity_square for the specified sixFunctorDirectIdentity.

Factor each compact-support comparison into the exact open realization square followed by the normalized direct-image comparison. The private generic paste_identity_units calculation uses naturality of the proper direct-image comparison and the two identity isomorphisms to paste open_identity_square and direct_identity_square. Expanding only the identity-factor and candidate unit definitions gives exactly identityFactorCoefficientComparison.

proof_origin.place: The original three-step coefficient identity-unit calculation, proved using generic adjunction transport and the existing all-complex inverse realization/direct-image normalization.

theorem identityFactorCoefficientComparison (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Z) (p : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsOpenImmersion i] [IsProper p]
    (M : DerivedCategory
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)))) :
    (sfIntrinsicCompactSupport (Compactification.ofIsProper p) A).map
        ((sfIntrinsicCompactSupportComparison A
          (Compactification.ofIsOpenImmersion i)).hom.app M) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicCompactSupportComparison A (Compactification.ofIsProper p)).hom.app
        ((sfFixedCompactSupport A (Compactification.ofIsOpenImmersion i)).obj M) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence Y A).functor.map
        ((identityFactorFixedIso (ULift.{u + 1} A) i p).hom.app M) =
    (sixFunctorProperCandidateIso A p).hom.app
        ((sfIntrinsicCompactSupport (Compactification.ofIsOpenImmersion i) A).obj
          ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X A).functor.obj M)) ≫
      (proEtaleConstantDerivedDirectImage p A).map
        ((sixFunctorOpenCandidateIso A i).hom.app
          ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X A).functor.obj M)) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicCompactSupportComparison A (identityFactorPair i p)).hom.app M
